text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Centre for Social Studies (CIS) strikes all political questions from September survey to lower tensions.
- Head of Basque government Jose Antonio Ardanza says state will lose legitimacy if it does not approve repatriation of imprisoned Basque separatist rebels.
- Pneumonia outbreak in Alcala is largest registered in Spain.
- Catalan financier Javier de la Rosa admits he took commissions from buyers and sellers at Grand Tibidado.
- Exchequer demands total nine billion pesetas from football clubs Barca and Real Madrid.
EL MUNDO

- Xabier Arzalluz, president of moderate Basque Nationalist Party (PNV), asks government to negotiate with ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) for freedom of prison officer Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, kidnapped nine months ago.
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar will meet Socialist opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez to discuss Spain's full entry into NATO.
DIARIO 16
- Former Civil Guard director Luis Roldan is depressed, asks for psychiatrist and wants to be released from jail.
ABC
- Madrid, capital of all protests, should have special zone for demonstrations.
CINCO DIAS
- Competition tribunal wants to cut commercial margins in sectors like books and pharmaceuticals.
- Teutonic rigor chills markets as Spanish bonds fall after Bundesbank member Hans-Juergen Koebnick says he doubts Spain and Italy will be among first EMU members.
- Government will probably have to privatise Telefonica in January.
- Argentaria to welcome members of former Banesto families.
EXPANSION
- Government selects Rothschild as consultant on Telefonica privatisation.
- Business association criticises 1997 budget.
- Planet Hollywood lands in Madrid next to Hard Rock Cafe with one billion peseta restaurant.
- Brussels fixes rules to maintain budget rigour after 1999.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Development minister announces law to ease private investment in public works.
- United Kingdom leads Europe in reducing unemployment.
- Director of state television Monica Ridruejo requests funds to finance urgent measures.
- State carrier Iberia responds to private firms with more flights and better prices.
